checks: For z≤0 the conditional negative-phase tail multiplies exp(z/r) by E[exp(−(aE₁+bE₂)/r)]=r²/[(a+r)(b+r)]. For z≥0 integration of the two-positive-phase survival at z+rE₃ multiplies its two exponentials by a/(a+r) and b/(b+r), respectively.

For a≠b the right-hand value at zero is (ab+r(a+b))/[(a+r)(b+r)], and its first and second z derivatives there are −r/[(a+r)(b+r)] and −1/[(a+r)(b+r)]. These equal the left-hand expressions. The integral of the scale derivative along the segment from b to a is smooth in positive parameters, so these identities persist at a=b and may be differentiated to give all mixed boundary matches of total order at most two.

On a compact parameter neighborhood bounded away from zero, the divided-difference integral and both exponential expressions have a uniform exponential bound times polynomials in |z| for their nonconstant terms through second order. Conditioning on the remaining phases therefore gives a quadratic integrable bound in their exponential sum, including when some of their coefficients are zero or change sign. With d=2 there are no remaining phases, and the same smooth survival kernel directly applies at z=0.

The identity P(λc)=P(c) for λ>0 first gives g·c=0, and differentiating the latter gives Hc=−g. For the actual section centroid, P(c)=F_{−c}(0) gives the positive sign g_j=f_{c·U}(0)b_j by proper-cut first variation. The independent shape-(d+1) gamma radius has E[G⁻¹]=1/d. Bounded coarea density and continuity at zero justify identifying f_V(0) with f_{c·U}(0)/d via the mixture and the continuous density version.
